subject: Hosted API capacity scenarios & budget check — Lumina Health
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@luminahealth.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API capacity scenarios & budget check — Lumina Health

Hi Olivia — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick written recap from our discovery so we can align on pricing/size options before I share a formal proposal. Please confirm or correct any numbers below.

Call highlights / Redwood reading of the scope:
- Primary use case: real-time patient intake summaries + eligibility checks (short prompts, frequent).
- Expected monthly token volume (initial 3–6 months): 20–40M tokens/month (conservative to aggressive).
- Target steady-state 12 TPS average for peak windows; short spikes up to ~18 TPS for 2–3 minute bursts during morning syncs.
- Desired target price: ~900 USD / 1M tokens (budgeted target for procurement).
- Other constraints: PHI in payloads (covered by our Business Associate Agreement), 12-month retention policy, and EU patients routed to their EU region (later phase).

What I need from you to finalize an options sheet:
1) Confirm the monthly token range (20–40M) and whether you expect >40M within 6 months.
2) Confirm peak TPS behavior (is 18 TPS spike ceiling correct and how often?).
3) Share any hard budget ceiling for unit economics (e.g., max $/1M tokens you can accept).
4) If you have a traffic matrix (tokens by hour/day), drop it here — that helps with recommended batching/latency tradeoffs.

Action items and immediate next steps:
- I will send two pricing paths: (A) 3-month committed slab with burst buffer (best $/1M), (B) On-demand with auto-burst (higher unit cost).
- Karthik (cc’d) will sketch throughput test steps and a rough unit-econ calc to validate your $900/1M target.
- If numbers check out, I’ll include an SOW template and a proposed rollout plan (canary by region + prefix caching).

Attachments: redwood-pricing-sheet-v2.xlsx (initial template we use for modeling)

Thanks — appreciate the clarity.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

From: Olivia Chen <olivia@luminahealth.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity scenarios & budget check — Lumina Health

Thanks Vanessa — confirm on most of this. Couple of clarifications from our side:

- Monthly tokens: conservative 25M, expected ramp to ~45M by month 6 if adoption goes well. So please model both 25M and 45M scenarios.
- Peak TPS: the 12 TPS average during mornings is accurate; we see ~16–18 TPS spikes for 3–5 minutes 2–3 times per morning (coincides with scheduled batch submissions). Spikes are short but fairly regular.
- Budget: procurement is comfortable with up to $1,000 / 1M tokens but we’d prefer something nearer $800–900 if possible — $900 is an OK stretch target.
- Security/compliance: we’ll need confirmation that data in transit + at rest is within our BAA and keys can be managed via our KMS. Also need SOC 2 attestation and a simple audit log export during pilot.

Attaching a small traffic matrix (lumina-traffic-matrix-may2027.csv) that shows hourly token distribution — hope this helps with batching recommendations.

Next steps from our side: Once we have a pricing sketched we’ll route to procurement and legal; procurement likes seeing a committed slab option with a burst buffer and clear overage math.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Olivia
Director of Engineering, Lumina Health
olivia@luminahealth.ai

Internal note / summary for pricing deck: forwarding Olivia’s confirm. Karthik — can you please do two quick artifacts by EOD so I can package into a proposal for procurement?

Requested artifacts:
- Unit economics calc for both 25M and 45M token scenarios, assuming: (A) committed 6-month slab + 20% burst buffer, (B) on-demand with 30% higher unit cost. Target to show cost at $800/$900/$1000 per 1M token to illustrate procurement options.
- Peak TPS validation: recommended instance sizing and suggestions for prefix KV caching and batching settings to keep 95th percentile latency < 300ms for the 16–18 TPS spikes.

I’ve added the ask re: SOC 2 and KMS to the attachments/notes we’ll include in the proposal. I’ll draft the SOW template (lightweight) once we land on a pricing band.

Attachments: sow-template-lumina-draft.pdf

Thanks —
V

Vanessa / Marissa — quick pass attached. I ran the numbers in the attached spreadsheet and sketched throughput sizing:

Quick summary (ballpark):
- 25M tokens/mo scenario:
  - Committed slab cost at $900 / 1M => ~$22,500 / month; with 20% burst buffer estimated infra + ops premium, effective cost "all-in" ~ $27k/mo.
  - On-demand (30% premium) => ~$29,250 / month.
- 45M tokens/mo scenario:
  - Committed slab at $900 / 1M => ~$40,500 / month; with buffer => ~$48k/mo.
  - On-demand => ~$52.5k/mo.

Throughput notes:
- To handle 18 TPS short spikes while keeping 95p latency < 300ms we recommend: 2x medium GPU workers with continuous batching + KV prefix caching; if you want headroom for sustained growth use 3x during morning windows with autoscale.
- Batching/window knobs: 20–40ms batch window on average traffic; increase to 60ms during spike windows if latency can tolerate (saves ~12% tokens).

I attached redwood-pricing-sheet-v2.xlsx with the calc tabs (scenario, infra-sizing, and legal notes for procurement). I also added a short blurb we can paste into the procurement email explaining burst math and overage caps.

Next: Vanessa — happy to prep a clean slide for procurement. Should I include the $800/1M sensitivity if you want to show upside?

—
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
